desc:
Custom API and backend development gives your site or app the hidden engine it runs on: a database, secure endpoints and background jobs. Ecom Swift LLC designs, builds, tests and deploys that engine in Node.js or Python, with documentation your front end team can use at once.

## What is a custom API and backend?

A custom API is the set of web addresses your site or app calls to read and change data, and the backend is everything behind those addresses: the database, the business rules and the scheduled work. Your front end, whether a website, a mobile app or a partner system, asks the API for information and the API answers. Without it, every screen has to fake its data or depend on a tool that was never built for your process.

## Why a well-built backend matters

Most product problems that look like front end bugs start in the backend. Data saved in the wrong shape, endpoints that return too much, and slow queries all show up later as broken screens and angry users. A backend built without authentication also exposes customer records to anyone who guesses a web address.

A clear data model and a documented API also let several people work at once. Your designer can build screens against the documentation while the endpoints are still being finished, and a future developer can read the code without guessing what each route does.

## How the backend affects your product and your costs

A backend does not generate leads by itself, but it decides how fast and how reliably everything else works. Fast endpoints make pages feel instant. Input validation stops bad data from entering your database, which saves hours of cleanup. Background jobs move slow work, such as sending emails or building reports, out of the request so users never wait for it.

It also affects cost. A tidy data model keeps queries cheap, so hosting stays small for longer. Logging and alerts mean you hear about errors from your own dashboard instead of from customers.

## What a great API and backend includes

- A data model drawn from how your business actually works, with clear relationships between records.
- Endpoints named and structured consistently, so they are easy to guess and easy to document.
- Token based authentication, with roles and permissions where different users need different access.
- Input validation on every request, so malformed or hostile data is rejected early.
- Rate limiting to protect the API from abuse and accidental floods.
- A queue for slow tasks such as email, file processing or exports.
- Error logging and alerts, so failures are visible within minutes.
- Hosted API documentation with example requests and responses.
- Automated tests on the endpoints that matter most.
- Secrets kept in environment settings, never written into the code.

## What we do

We start by talking through your product and drawing the data model with you: what the records are, who owns them and how they relate. Then we build the database and the endpoints in Node.js or Python, whichever suits your team, and protect them with authentication.

We write the documentation as we go, so your front end developer does not have to wait. Tests cover the main paths, and we deploy the finished API to your own hosting account. The Basic package covers a small API for one core resource. Standard widens it to several resources, roles and a background job. Premium adds queues, rate limiting, logging with alerts and a walkthrough of the code.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe real situations your users face, not only a list of screens.
- Decide early who can see and change which records.
- Keep a list of other systems the API must talk to.
- Plan for a staging copy so you can test changes safely.
- Ask for the documentation to be reviewed by whoever will build the front end.

**Avoid:**
- Putting business rules only in the front end, where users can bypass them.
- Returning every field of a record when a screen needs three.
- Skipping validation because the data currently comes from a trusted form.
- Sharing one admin key between every person and system.
- Treating logging as something to add after launch.

## Who this is for

This service suits a founder whose prototype runs on spreadsheets and needs a real database behind it. It suits a business with a website that must feed orders, bookings or users into an internal system. It also suits a front end team that has designed the screens but has nothing to connect them to.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of what the product should do, who will use it and any existing data or systems it must connect with. We need a hosting account you own, and access as a developer user or collaborator where the host supports it. We never need your passwords. After you order, we reply with a short list of questions and keep you updated until the API is deployed and documented.
